title.narrative: Activity under preparation ACT-63750 Support for Digitalisation of critical institutions to improve the business environment in Bolivia

description.narrative: The Plurinational State of Bolivia faces growing challenges linked to digital infrastructure that lags behind regional standards, with implications for both economic competitiveness and cybersecurity. While the digitalisation of public services is a government priority, it requires a robust framework to protect critical infrastructure from cyber threats and to ensure data sovereignty. Strengthening key State institutions, as well as security and border management systems, will help improve the business environment, reinforce transparency and accountability, and support Bolivia¿s integration into regional and global markets.The action will support Bolivia¿s digital transformation strategy by promoting digital public administration, interoperability and cybersecurity. A specific focus will be placed on cybersecurity and on the digitalisation of institutional tools for the investigation of, and fight against transnational organised crime, with particular emphasis on illicit trafficking in controlled substances, corruption and related crimes. The action will also strengthen interoperability across the law-enforcement, prosecution and judicial chain. It will support the development of the existing national cybersecurity capabilities through the establishment of a Government Security Operations Centre (SOC) supporting the Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT), hosted by the Agencia de Gobierno Electrónico y Tecnologías de Información y Comunicación (AGETIC) and developed with strategic technical support from Spain¿s Centro Criptológico Nacional (CCN), mobilised through Fundación para la Internacionalización de las Administraciones Públicas (FIAP) as the pillar-assesed and technically relevant implementing partner. . The SOC is expected to provide continuous security monitoring, threat detection, incident response support and operational threat intelligence for prioritised public institutions while laying the foundations for the gradual expansion of national cybersecurity capabilities in line with EU cybersecurity standards such as NIS2 Directive and the Cybersecurity Act. The new SOC will operate in direct coordination with Bolivia's established CSIRT to ensure aligned response efforts.The initiative will contribute to the design, development and implementation of an Integrated Information Security Ecosystem for the Bolivian Police. This ecosystem will modernise the processes for registering, managing, analysing and exchanging information of relevance to police work. It will support data integration, advanced criminal analysis, institutional interoperability, traceability of procedures, and the generation of evidence to inform evidence-based public policies and strengthen the prosecution of organised crime. It will also reinforce standards for digital governance, data protection, cybersecurity and institutional transparency, which will be based on existing EU frameworks such as NIS2 Directive, GDPR and Interoperable Europe Act.The action will include a component aimed at strengthening the security architecture and regional integration through the harmonisation and progressive incorporation of the regulatory frameworks of MERCOSUR and the Andean Community (CAN) in relation to integrated border management, the fight against organised crime, and anti-corruption efforts. Within this framework, digital infrastructure will be developed to facilitate secure cross-border cooperation and interoperability with the information platforms and systems of MERCOSUR and CAN member countries, thereby promoting timely information exchange and regional operational cooperation.
